answer: In an AI-agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to complete a unique computational voyage whose intermediate states are sealed inside a personal vault protected by a non-transferable cryptographic relic. An attacker wanting multiple identities must expend fresh CPU-hours and energy for every fake agent, because the voyage cannot be parallelized or reused; the vault refuses to open for any replica that lacks the exact relic generated during that specific run, raising the marginal cost linearly with the number of sybils.
